Google Sheets add-ons take over the tasks you'd otherwise handle by hand, like pulling data from other apps, cleaning up messy columns, and sending outreach one row at a time.

## What is a Google Sheets add-on


A Google Sheets add-on is


a third-party app you install from the


[Google Workspace Marketplace](https://workspace.google.com/marketplace) that runs inside your spreadsheet


. Most show up as a sidebar or a new menu item, and some add new functions you can type straight into a cell.


Under the hood, they’re built on Google Apps Script, which is how they


[read, format, and act on your data](https://developers.google.com/workspace/add-ons/editors/sheets) .


💡


Note:


Add-ons and extensions are not the same thing, even though Google files add-ons under the Extensions menu. Add-ons install from the Marketplace and run inside Sheets. Browser extensions install in your browser from a browser store. This article is only about add-ons.


## How I researched and tested these Google Sheets add-ons


I installed each add-on from the Google Workspace Marketplace and ran it against real reporting, cleanup, and outreach tasks I already had on my plate.


Here's what I considered:


-


Job it solves:


Whether the add-on handles a spreadsheet problem Sheets can't already solve on its own.


-


Setup time:


How long it took to go from install to a working result.


-


Permissions requested:


Whether the access it asked for matched the job it does.


-


Maintenance and reviews:


How recently it was updated and how it handles bugs users report.


Testing these side by side taught me something simple: an add-on that solves one job well beats one that tries to do five jobs at once.

## 1. Supermetrics: Best for pulling marketing and sales data into a sheet


-


What it does:


[Supermetrics](https://workspace.google.com/marketplace/app/supermetrics/523876908005) is a marketing data connector that pulls campaign and analytics data from over 150 platforms directly into a spreadsheet.


-


Best for:


Marketers and agencies reporting across several ad platforms who want the numbers in one sheet without a manual export.


-


Rating:


4.4/5, ~958 reviews


-


Downloads:


1M+


Supermetrics is built around direct connections to marketing and sales platforms, so I connected a Google Ads account and pulled a month of campaign spend into a blank sheet to see how much manual exporting it removed.


I picked a data source, chose my metrics and date range,


and watched the numbers populate within a few minutes


. The setup took longer than expected once I added a second platform, since each connector needs its own separate login and permissions.


### Key features


-


[Wide connector library](https://supermetrics.com/connectors) :


Supermetrics connects to over 150 marketing, sales, and analytics platforms, including Google Analytics, Google Ads, and major social channels.


-


Scheduled refreshes:


Reports update on a schedule you set, without a manual re-export.


-


Prebuilt report templates:


Premade templates give you a starting layout for common reports.


### Pros and cons


✅ Pros


❌ Cons


Removes manual exports across many data sources


Priced per connector, so costs add up with multiple platforms


Scheduled refreshes keep a report current without manual work


Each new connector needs its own separate login and setup


Premade templates cut setup time for common reports


### Pricing


Supermetrics offers a free trial of its add-on, then starts at


[$44 per month](https://supermetrics.com/pricing) .


### Bottom line


Supermetrics carries the deepest connector library of any add-on on this list, which matters most once your reporting spans more than one or two ad platforms. If you only need to sync a single app on a schedule, Coupler.io is worth checking instead.


## 2. Coupler.io: Best for scheduled imports that refresh on their own


-


What it does:


[Coupler.io](https://workspace.google.com/marketplace/app/couplerio/532272210531) is a data import tool that pulls records from apps like Airtable, Shopify, and HubSpot into a spreadsheet on a set schedule.


-


Best for:


Finance, ecommerce, and ops teams who need a report that stays current without anyone remembering to refresh it.


-


Rating:


4.8/5, ~279 reviews


-


Downloads:


427K+


To see how Coupler.io handled a recurring report, I set up an import from a sample sales source and ran it on the free plan first.


Refreshes are manual, so I had to click refresh myself each time to get the updates


.


Moving to the Starter plan is what unlocks daily auto-refresh, and that's the tier where the set-and-forget value actually kicks in.


### Key features


-


Scheduled imports:


Refresh data hourly, daily, or on specific days of the week.


-


Multi-app support:


Connect popular business apps without writing scripts.


-


Combined sources:


Pull data from more than one account into a single sheet.


### Pros and cons


✅ Pros


❌ Cons


Set-and-forget data syncing once configured


Advanced scheduling frequencies sit behind paid plans


No code or scripts required to connect an app


Source list is smaller than Supermetrics for marketing platforms


Works across more than one account in a single import


### Pricing


Coupler.io offers a free plan, then starts at


[$24 per month](https://www.coupler.io/pricing) .


### Bottom line


Coupler.io covers a broader mix of business apps than marketing-only connectors, which matters if your reporting pulls from finance or ecommerce tools. For syncing data between several sheets and departments, consider Sheetgo.


## 3. Power Tools: Best for cleaning and reformatting messy sheets


-


What it does:


[Power Tools](https://workspace.google.com/marketplace/app/power_tools/1058867473888) is a spreadsheet cleanup add-on that bundles dozens of formatting and data utilities into one sidebar.


-


Best for:


Anyone who inherits a messy spreadsheet and needs to fix inconsistent formatting fast,


[without writing a formula](https://julius.ai/articles/google-sheets-ai-formula) for each fix.


-


Rating:


3.6/5, ~2,140 reviews


-


Downloads:


8M+


I tested Power Tools on a sheet full of inconsistent capitalization and stray whitespace, since it bundles dozens of cleanup utilities into one sidebar.


Jobs that would normally mean digging through menus or writing a formula took fewer clicks


. If your usual fix is manually cleaning columns and trying to


[remove duplicate rows in Google Sheets](https://julius.ai/articles/how-to-remove-duplicates-google-sheets) , this puts it all in one place.


The interface took me a few minutes to get used to, since the sidebar packs in a lot of options.


### Key features


-


Cleanup toolkit:


Remove duplicates, trim spaces, and fix casing in a click.


-


Split and merge:


Break names into columns or combine cells without formulas.


-


Bulk formatting:


Apply repetitive formatting across templated workbooks.


### Pros and cons


✅ Pros


❌ Cons


Replaces a stack of one-off cleanup formulas


Full toolkit sits behind a paid plan after the trial


Broad set of utilities in a single sidebar


Interface takes some time to learn given how many options it packs in


Handles bulk formatting across templated sheets


### Pricing


Power Tools offers a free trial, then starts at


[$49.99 per year](https://www.ablebits.com/google-sheets-add-ons/power-tools/index.php) .


### Bottom line


Power Tools packs more cleanup utilities into a single sidebar than any other tool on this list, so it earns its keep if cleaning data is a regular part of your week. If your bigger problem is connecting outside data sources, Supermetrics or Coupler.io are worth a look instead.


## 4. AppSheet: Best for building a no-code app on your sheet


-


What it does:


[AppSheet](https://workspace.google.com/marketplace/app/appsheet/376242260902) is a no-code app builder that turns spreadsheet data into a working mobile or web app.


-


Best for:


Field teams and small businesses that want a lightweight app layered on top of data they already track in a sheet.


-


Rating:


4.4/5, ~1,322 reviews


-


Downloads:


28M+


AppSheet lets you turn a spreadsheet into a working app without any coding, so I connected a sample inventory sheet and let it generate a basic app around the existing columns.


The result came with working forms and views out of the box


, and I could customize fields to add image capture for each inventory item.


Adjusting the app's layout took some trial and error, since the builder has more settings than a typical add-on and I had to hunt for the ones that mattered.


### Key features


-


No-code app building:


Turn spreadsheet rows into a usable app automatically.


-


Mobile data capture:


Collect text, images, and signatures in the field.


-


Templates:


Start from prebuilt app patterns and adjust them to fit your workflow.


### Pros and cons


✅ Pros


❌ Cons


Real app functionality built without writing code


Learning curve is steeper than a typical add-on


Backed and maintained directly by Google


Publishing to more users moves you onto a paid plan


Mobile forms support image and signature capture in the field


### Pricing


AppSheet is free to build and share with a small group, then starts at


[$5 per user per month](https://about.appsheet.com/pricing/) to publish to more users.


### Bottom line


AppSheet is the only tool on this list that turns a sheet into a working app. If you just need to visualize existing rows in a browsable format, Awesome Table is a lighter option to reach for.


## 5. Yet Another Mail Merge: Best for sending personalized email from a sheet


-


What it does:


[Yet Another Mail Merge](https://workspace.google.com/marketplace/app/yet_another_mail_merge_mail_merge_for_gm/52669349336) is a Gmail mail merge tool that sends personalized emails using contacts and templates stored in a sheet.


-


Best for:


Recruiters, founders, and outreach teams sending a list-driven email campaign straight from their own Gmail account.


-


Rating:


4.7/5, ~18,152 reviews


-


Downloads:


16M+


I tested Yet Another Mail Merge by building a short contact list and Gmail template, then running a test merge to check the personalization and tracking.


Each email arrived with the correct name pulled from its row


, and the sheet showed me open and click data within minutes.


Setting up the template took some patience, since mapping each column meant checking the draft closely before sending. The free plan capped me at a small number of daily sends, so a bigger list means a paid tier.


### Key features


-


Gmail sending:


Send from your own Gmail address instead of a third-party platform.


-


Personalization:


Map any column into the message body.


-


Tracking:


See opens and clicks reported back in the sheet.


### Pros and cons


✅ Pros


❌ Cons


Sends stay inside Gmail and Sheets, no separate platform needed


Daily send limits apply, especially on the free plan


Open and click tracking built directly into the sheet


Initial template setup takes some trial and error


Personalization pulls straight from existing spreadsheet columns


### Pricing


Yet Another Mail Merge offers a free plan, then starts at


[$72 per year](https://yamm.com/pricing/) .


### Bottom line


Yet Another Mail Merge keeps outreach tracking inside the same sheet you're already sending from. For a larger contact list that needs conditional logic on when each email goes out, Form Mule is worth a look instead.


## 6. Awesome Table: Best for turning rows into a browsable interface


-


What it does:


[Awesome Table](https://workspace.google.com/marketplace/app/awesome_table/56088344336) is a data visualization add-on that turns a range of spreadsheet rows into a filterable table, card, or map view.


-


Best for:


Teams that want to share spreadsheet data with people who don't want to dig through a raw grid.


-


Rating:


4.6/5, ~547 reviews


-


Downloads:


13M+


To test Awesome Table's


[data visualization](https://julius.ai/articles/google-sheets-data-visualization) chops, I pointed it at a spreadsheet of contact entries and switched between table, card, and map views.


I got dropdown filters and a search bar without writing a single formula


, and the map view plotted every entry by address on its own.


Some settings sit in a separate panel from the main preview, and the free tier capped how many rows I could import before truncating results.


### Key features


-


Multiple views:


Display data as tables, cards, maps, or Gantt-style layouts.


-


Built-in filtering:


Give viewers dropdowns and sliders to explore the data.


-


Shareable interface:


Publish a browsable view instead of the raw sheet.


### Pros and cons


✅ Pros


❌ Cons


Makes spreadsheet data approachable for non-technical viewers


Free tier caps how many rows you can import


Multiple view types beyond a plain grid


You may need to dig around for some settings


Filtering and search work without writing formulas


### Pricing


Awesome Table offers a free plan, then starts at


[$16 per month](https://awesome-table.com/pricing) .


### Bottom line


Awesome Table turns a spreadsheet into something a non-spreadsheet person can browse, with dropdown filters and a search bar doing the work a raw grid can't. If your goal is a diagram or flowchart, Lucidchart handles that work better.


## 7. Lucidchart: Best for adding diagrams and flowcharts to a sheet


-


What it does:


[Lucidchart](https://workspace.google.com/marketplace/app/lucidchart/7081045131) is a diagramming add-on that brings flowcharts, org charts, and wireframes into a spreadsheet.


-


Best for:


Teams that need process diagrams and flowcharts beyond the basic bar and line charts Sheets includes.


-


Rating:


4.1/5, ~9,958 reviews


-


Downloads:


46M+


I built a simple flowchart in Lucidchart and imported it alongside a linked spreadsheet to check whether it could bring a real process diagram into a working sheet.


The diagram carried over cleanly


, and I could open the linked sheet from inside Lucidchart without switching tabs.


Lucidchart can auto-generate org charts directly from spreadsheet data, but flowcharts don't work the same way, so I had to build mine from scratch. If you're mapping a process, plan on starting from a blank canvas.


### Key features


-


Advanced diagrams:


Flowcharts, wireframes, and organizational charts.


-


Two-way linking:


Access linked spreadsheets from inside Lucidchart.


-


Collaboration:


Share and co-edit diagrams with your team.


### Pros and cons


✅ Pros


❌ Cons


Far more diagram options than Sheets' built-in charts


Doesn't auto-generate flowcharts from spreadsheet data, only org charts


Two-way linking keeps the diagram and the sheet connected


Free plan caps documents and shapes


Useful for process and structure visuals a chart can't show


### Pricing


Lucidchart offers a free plan, then starts at


[$9 per month](https://lucid.app/pricing/lucidchart#/pricing/chart) .


### Bottom line


Lucidchart handles process and structure diagrams that Sheets' native charts can't touch. If you want a browsable view of your data instead, Awesome Table is worth checking out.


## 8. Form Publisher: Best for turning rows into Docs, Slides, or PDFs


-


What it does:


[Form Publisher](https://workspace.google.com/marketplace/app/form_publisher/827172627657) is a document automation add-on that generates Google Docs, Slides, PDFs, or Word files from spreadsheet rows using a template you set up once.


-


Best for:


HR, education, and operations teams producing many similar documents from the same data source.


-


Rating:


4.6/5, ~4,269 reviews


-


Downloads:


24M+


I built a template with a few marker fields, then generated a document for each row in a test sheet to see if Form Publisher could turn repetitive paperwork into a time saver.


Every document I opened had the correct fields filled in


, and I found a link back to each finished file waiting in the sheet.


Building the template took significant effort at first, since I had to place every marker precisely and test a sample row before running the full batch. The free plan also capped how many documents I could generate monthly.


### Key features


-


Template-driven output:


Generate a formatted file for every row.


-


Multiple formats:


Produce Docs, Slides, PDFs, or Word files.


-


Linked results:


Drop a link to each generated file back in the sheet.


### Pros and cons


✅ Pros


❌ Cons


Automates document creation for repetitive batches


Initial template setup takes real effort


Handles several output formats from one template


Free tier caps monthly document generation


Links back to every finished file inside the sheet


### Pricing


Form Publisher offers a free plan, then starts at


[$99 per year](https://form-publisher.com/pricing/) .


### Bottom line


Form Publisher turns a template and a row of data into a finished document without any manual copy-paste. If you need to merge rows into a document that also updates other apps on a schedule, Sheetgo is worth checking out.


## 9. Sheetgo: Best for automating workflows between sheets


-


What it does:


[Sheetgo](https://workspace.google.com/marketplace/app/sheetgo/94172092257) is a workflow automation add-on that connects multiple spreadsheets into a pipeline so data flows between them automatically.


-


Best for:


Organizations where different teams each own a sheet that needs to roll up into one master file.


-


Rating:


4.2/5, ~1,793 reviews


-


Downloads:


5M+


I linked two department sheets to see if Sheetgo could handle a rollup without any manual copy-paste.


The connection merged both sheets into a single master file on the schedule I set,


and I watched a new row from one source sheet show up in the master file within minutes.


Setting up the first connection took some trial and error, since I had to match column headers exactly across both sheets before the merge would run cleanly.


### Key features


-


Connected pipelines:


Link sheets so data flows automatically between them.


-


Consolidation:


Merge multiple sheets into a single master file.


-


Scheduling:


Refresh connections on a set schedule.


### Pros and cons


✅ Pros


❌ Cons


Solves the multi-sheet rollup problem without scripts


Free plan caps how many connections you can run


Scheduled syncs keep a master file current on their own


Column headers need to match exactly across sheets before merging


Works across sheets owned by different teams


### Pricing


Sheetgo offers a free plan, then starts at


[$35 per month](https://www.sheetgo.com/pricing/automations/) .


### Bottom line


Sheetgo solves the specific problem of pulling scattered, team-owned sheets into one place on a schedule. If your bottleneck is building a contact list, Hunter for Sheets is worth checking out.


## 10. Hunter for Sheets: Best for finding and verifying email addresses


-


What it does:


[Hunter for Sheets](https://workspace.google.com/marketplace/app/hunter_for_sheets/327237705162) is an email lookup add-on that finds and verifies professional email addresses directly inside a spreadsheet.


-


Best for:


Sales and recruiting teams building or cleaning up an outreach list.


-


Rating:


4.4/5, ~163 reviews


-


Downloads:


57K+


I fed Hunter a short list of company domains to see how usable the results would be for a real outreach list.


The add-on returned likely email addresses for each domain within a few minutes


, and I ran a separate column of existing addresses through its verification check to see a deliverability score for each one.


Connecting Hunter meant creating a separate account and signing in before the sidebar would run any lookups. The free plan capped me at a small number of monthly searches, so a bigger list means moving to a paid tier.


### Key features


-


Email lookup:


Find addresses from a company domain.


-


Verification:


Score existing addresses for how likely they are to be valid.


-


In-sheet workflow:


Work from the spreadsheet you already use.


### Pros and cons


✅ Pros


❌ Cons


Combines finding and verifying addresses in one sidebar


Requires connecting a separate Hunter account


Keeps list building inside the sheet you already use


Free tier has a low monthly search cap


Verification scores flag risky addresses before you send


### Pricing


Hunter for Sheets offers a free plan, then starts at


[$408 per year](https://hunter.io/pricing) .


### Bottom line


Hunter for Sheets combines finding and verifying addresses in one sidebar, a pairing none of the other outreach tools on this list handle together. For sending the actual campaign once you've built your list, Yet Another Mail Merge picks up where this leaves off.


## Special mentions


A few more add-ons came up during research that didn't earn a full section but are worth a quick look.


Each one solves a narrower job than the add-ons above:


1.


ChangeCase is a text-formatting add-on, and I ran it on a column of inconsistently capitalized entries to fix the case in one pass. It offers sentence case and invert case beyond the usual upper, lower, and title case options, but it only touches text case, so anything messier still needs a separate cleanup pass.


2.


Crop Sheet takes a narrow approach to cleanup, and I used it to trim a sheet down to just its used data so stray rows and columns stopped cluttering the view. One limitation is it only crops, so duplicates or formatting still need another tool.


3.

Installing an add-on takes about a minute on desktop.

Install

Launch or open its sidebar to run it


.


To remove an add-on


, go to Extensions > Add-ons > Manage add-ons, click the three-dot menu next to it, and choose Uninstall.


Add-ons don't run on the native mobile apps for Sheets


. Neither Android nor iPhone/iPad support the add-on sidebar, so full access requires a desktop browser, or a mobile browser forced into desktop view.


If the Extensions menu looks missing or greyed out, you're likely in a view-only file, your Google Workspace admin has restricted add-ons, or you're on a mobile app that doesn't support them. Opening a sheet you own on desktop should bring the menu back.

## Frequently asked questions


### Are Google Sheets add-ons free?


Many Google Sheets add-ons are free


, though tools like Supermetrics and Power Tools switch to a paid plan after a free trial. Check each add-on's pricing before you install, since free tiers often cap usage.


### Are Google Sheets add-ons safe to install?


Yes, well-reviewed Google Sheets add-ons from the Google Workspace Marketplace are safe


to install. Look for Google's verification signals, read the permissions each add-on requests before clicking Allow, and uninstall anything you stop using.


### Why is the Extensions menu missing in Google Sheets?


The Extensions menu goes missing


when you're in a view-only file


,


when a Google Workspace admin has restricted add-ons


, or when you're on a mobile app that doesn't support them. Opening a sheet you own on desktop brings the menu back.


### What is the difference between a Google Sheets add-on and an extension?


Google Sheets add-ons


install from the Google Workspace Marketplace and run inside Sheets under the Extensions menu, while


browser extensions


install in a web browser and aren't specific to Sheets. The two terms get mixed up because Google files both under the same menu name.


### Can you use Google Sheets add-ons on mobile?


No, not on the native mobile apps


. Neither the Android nor iOS Google Sheets app supports the add-on sidebar. You’ll need to use Sheets on a desktop browser, or a mobile browser forced into desktop mode.
